name: HAYSTAC

physics_goals.quote: The Haloscope At Yale Sensitive To Axion CDM (HAYSTAC) Experiment is a microwave cavity search for cold dark matter (CDM) axions with masses above 20ueV.
physics_goals.value: Search for cold dark matter axions with masses above 20 ueV via resonant conversion to photons in a magnetic field

summary.plain: HAYSTAC searches for the axion, a candidate dark-matter particle, at Yale University. A tunable metal cavity inside a strong magnet, cooled and read out with quantum-noise-reducing electronics, listens for a faint radio signal the axion would produce.
summary.technical: Tunable microwave-cavity haloscope at Yale Wright Laboratory searching for cold dark-matter axions above 20 ueV via inverse-Primakoff conversion in a static magnetic field; Phase II uses a squeezed-vacuum receiver for sub-quantum-limited noise, having scanned 16.96-19.46 ueV combined as of 2024-2025 data.

unique_capabilities.quote: It represents the widest search to date that utilizes squeezing to realize sub-quantum limited noise.
unique_capabilities.value: Uses a squeezed-vacuum quantum receiver to beat the standard quantum noise limit and speed up the axion search
